content:
Visual communication enhances every aspect of your service—from worship lyrics that free people to lift their eyes, to sermon graphics that reinforce key points, to announcements that inform without taking stage time. This guide helps you select projection equipment that serves your portable church needs.

---

## Why Video Matters

### Worship Engagement

When lyrics are clear and readable, worshippers can focus on God rather than squinting at a screen or fumbling with a hymnal. Good projection enables participation.

### Communication Efficiency

Announcements, scripture references, and sermon points displayed visually reinforce verbal communication and reduce the need for lengthy explanations.

### Professional Impression

Clean, well-executed visuals communicate that your church cares about quality and pays attention to details—even in a temporary facility.

### Guest Accessibility

New guests may not know your songs or where to find scripture. On-screen display makes everyone an insider from their first visit.

<Callout type="tip">
  Video projection is about communication, not entertainment. Keep your focus on clarity and readability rather than flashy effects.
</Callout>

---

## System Components

A complete video projection system includes:

### Projector

The device that creates the image:

| Factor | Considerations |
|--------|---------------|
| **Brightness** | Measured in lumens—more is better for ambient light |
| **Resolution** | Choose resolution for text size and viewing distance |
| **Contrast** | Higher contrast improves readability |
| **Lens** | Zoom range affects placement flexibility |
| **Connectivity** | HDMI standard; multiple inputs helpful |

### Screen

The surface that displays the image:

| Type | Pros | Cons |
|------|------|------|
| **Tripod** | Portable, affordable | Size limits, stability issues |
| **Frame** | Tensioned, flat surface | Setup time, larger transport |
| **Drape** | Integrates with backdrop | Less reflective, lower contrast |
| **Wall** | No equipment needed | Color/texture issues |

### Playback Computer

The source for your content:

- **Presentation software:** ProPresenter, EasyWorship, MediaShout
- **Hardware:** Laptop with adequate graphics capability
- **Backup:** Secondary computer or backup content method

### Switching and Distribution

For multiple display scenarios:

- HDMI splitters for duplicate output
- HDMI switchers for multiple sources
- HDMI-over-Cat6 for long runs
- Signal boosters for extended distances

### Confidence Monitors

Displays for stage reference:

- Shows performers what the audience sees
- Enables pastor to reference notes without turning
- Can display countdown timers
- Typically LCD TVs on floor or low stands

---

## Selecting a Projector

### Brightness Requirements

Ambient light affects image visibility. Use these planning rules of thumb, then test in your venue:

| Environment | Brightness Planning |
|-------------|---------------------|
| Dark room, controlled lighting | Test at the intended screen size |
| Some ambient light | Allow more light output than in a dark room |
| Significant ambient light | Test brightness and contrast with the lights on |
| Windows, high ambient | Reduce light on the screen or compare other displays |

There is no single lumen range that suits most portable churches. Match brightness to your room, screen, and content.
### Projector Technologies

| Technology | Characteristics |
|------------|----------------|
| **LCD** | Image-forming technology; models may use lamps or lasers |
| **DLP** | Image-forming technology; design and light source vary by model |
| **Laser** | Light source, not an alternative to LCD or DLP; startup and cost vary by model |

Laser-lit projectors avoid routine lamp replacement; compare purchase price, rated light-source life, and maintenance for the specific model.

### Resolution and Aspect Ratio

- **1080p (1920x1080)** — A Full HD format option
- **4K UHD (3840x2160)** — Check whether your content and viewing distance benefit
- **16:9 aspect ratio** — A widescreen option; match your content and display

### Features to Prioritize

Essential:
- Adequate lumens for your venue
- Resolution suited to your content and viewing distance
- HDMI input
- Lens shift (vertical at minimum)
- Zoom lens for placement flexibility

Helpful:
- Multiple inputs
- Network control
- Quick startup/shutdown
- Horizontal lens shift
- Quiet operation

---

## Screen Selection

### Size Calculation

Screen should be large enough for back-row readability:

**Rule of thumb:** Size the image for the smallest text and the farthest viewer, then test back-row readability. AVIXA's display-size method considers image height, text/element height, and viewer positions.

| Screen Diagonal (16:9) | Approximate Image Width |
|-----------------------|-------------------------|
| 100" | 87" |
| 120" | 105" |
| 150" | 131" |
| 180" | 157" |

Err on the side of larger—text that's too small frustrates viewers.

### Screen Types for Portable Use

**Tripod Screens**
- Easiest to transport
- Check available sizes and transport dimensions
- Can be unstable
- Best for smaller venues

**Fast-Fold Frames**
- Professional appearance
- Larger sizes available
- More setup time
- Higher quality surface

**Pipe and Drape Integration**
- Hang a screen only from a support rated by its manufacturer for the load
- Flexible positioning
- Requires compatible screen material
- May need tensioning system

<Callout type="warning">
  As a purchasing rule of thumb, test wall color, texture, and viewing angles before relying on wall projection. Consider a proper screen if image quality is inadequate.
</Callout>

### Screen Surface Types

| Surface | Best For | Gain |
|---------|----------|------|
| **Matte white** | Wide viewing angles | Check model specification |
| **High contrast grey** | Contrast control; performance varies with room light | Check model specification |
| **High gain** | More on-axis brightness; check viewing angle | Check model specification |
| **Rear projection** | Projector behind the screen | Check model specification |

As a purchasing rule of thumb, compare screen surfaces in your actual lighting conditions.

---

## Confidence Monitors

### Purpose

Confidence monitors show presenters what the audience sees, plus additional information:

- Lyrics so worship leaders don't turn around
- Sermon notes for the pastor
- Countdown timers for service flow
- Stage directions or cues

### Common Configuration

These monitor sizes are planning examples; test text readability from each presenter's position.

| Location | Content | Size |
|----------|---------|------|
| Floor, center stage | Lyrics, notes | 40-55" |
| Side stage | Lyrics, cues | 32-40" |
| Back of room | Stage view | Optional |

### Equipment Options

- **LCD TVs** — Affordable, versatile, available everywhere
- **Dedicated monitors** — More robust for transport
- **Tablets** — Personal monitoring option

Presentation software such as EasyWorship supports separate audience and foldback outputs; confirm the outputs your chosen software supports.

---

## Playback and Software

### Presentation Software Options

| Software | Platform | Strengths |
|----------|----------|-----------|
| **ProPresenter** | Mac/Windows | Audience/stage outputs; test with your setup |
| **EasyWorship** | Mac/Windows | Worship presentation and foldback output |
| **MediaShout** | Mac/Windows; separate versions | Worship presentation |
| **OpenLP** | Cross-platform | Free, open-source worship presentation |
| **PowerPoint** | Mac/Windows | General presentation; test your worship workflow |

Compare presentation software with your own content and volunteers before purchasing. Platform listings checked October 16, 2026; confirm current system requirements with each vendor.

### Computer Requirements

Whatever software you choose:

- Dedicated computer (not dual-use)
- Storage that meets your chosen software's requirements
- RAM matched to the software, resolution, and number of outputs
- Graphics capability matched to your outputs; some systems use integrated graphics
- Multiple video outputs

### Backup Strategy

Always have a backup plan:

- Second computer with content loaded
- USB drive with exported content
- Printed lyrics for emergencies
- Clear handoff procedures

<Callout type="insight">
  The computer running lyrics is as critical as the projector. Treat it as essential equipment, not an afterthought.
</Callout>

---

## Signal Distribution

### Cable Types and Distances

| Cable Type | Distance Planning | Notes |
|------------|-------------------|-------|
| HDMI (passive) | Check the cable's rated format and length | Test resolution and refresh rate |
| HDMI (active) | Check the cable's rated format and length | Check direction and power needs |
| HDMI over Cat6 | Check extender and cable specifications | Requires compatible converters |
| SDI | Check cable, data rate, and equipment specifications | Requires SDI-compatible equipment |

As a purchasing rule of thumb, compare active HDMI and HDMI-over-Cat6 systems for your required signal format and cable length.

### Distribution Equipment

**HDMI Splitter**
- Takes one input, creates multiple identical outputs
- Useful for projector + confidence monitor
- Ensure HDCP compliance

**HDMI Switcher**
- Multiple inputs, one output
- Useful for computer + video source
- Can be manual or automatic

**Scalers/Converters**
- Convert between formats (VGA to HDMI, etc.)
- Scale resolution for compatibility
- Useful for legacy equipment

---

## Setup and Positioning

### Projector Placement

**Front projection** (projector on the audience side of the screen):
- Check throw distance and audience sightlines
- Requires clear throw path
- Projector may be in front of, above, or behind the audience
- Keystoning correction may be needed

**Rear projection** (projector behind screen):
- Cleaner look, no visible equipment
- Requires space behind screen
- Special screen material needed
- Check space and transport needs

### Avoiding Problems

| Problem | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| **Shadows on screen** | Keep people and equipment out of the projection path |
| **Keystone distortion** | Level projector, use lens shift |
| **Hot spots** | Choose appropriate screen gain |
| **Color accuracy** | Calibrate projector, check content |

### Screen Positioning

- Center screen for primary viewing
- Height allows clear sightlines
- Far enough from seating for wide viewing angle
- Consider dual screens for wide rooms

---

## Budget Considerations

### Sample Budget Ranges

| Component | Entry | Mid-Range | Professional |
|-----------|-------|-----------|--------------|
| Projector | Quote required | Quote required | Quote required |
| Screen (100-150") | Quote required | Quote required | Quote required |
| Playback computer | Quote required | Quote required | Quote required |
| Software | Quote required | Quote required | Quote required |
| Confidence monitors | Quote required | Quote required | Quote required |
| Cables/distribution | Quote required | Quote required | Quote required |
| **Total** | **Quote required** | **Quote required** | **Quote required** |

### Where to Invest

- **Projector brightness** — You can't add lumens later
- **Quality screen** — Dramatically affects image
- **Reliable cabling** — Failures are embarrassing

### Where to Save

- Confidence monitors (consumer TVs work fine)
- Computer (adequate is sufficient)
- Cases (functional over fancy)

---

## Training and Documentation

### Skills Your Team Needs

| Skill | Who |
|-------|-----|
| Basic operation | All video team |
| Content creation/editing | 1-2 people |
| Troubleshooting | Team leads |
| Setup/teardown | All team |

### Documentation to Create

- Setup diagram with cable routing
- Quick-start operating guide
- Troubleshooting flowchart
- Content creation guidelines

---

<Callout type="scripture">
  *"One thing I have asked from Yahweh, that I shall seek: That I may dwell in the house of Yahweh all the days of my life, To behold the beauty of Yahweh And to inquire in His temple."* — Psalm 27:4 (LSB)
</Callout>

Video projection is a tool for helping people see—not just the screen, but the God we worship. Choose equipment that serves that purpose well.
